pre_mortem: A strong solver fixes the seven departures (cut-off window, curve points, NTC cut-off, uncapped factor, median outliers, no substitution for not-detected, per-gene geometric-mean normalisation), writes a reference from the SOP and differentially fuzzes the package. Its reference must decide two values the SOP leaves open. (1) The mean Ct when every reportable replicate is an outlier: the median rule empties the set only for even counts with a wide middle gap, which tight self-generated replicates never produce; when it does appear, the reference crashes or routes it to 'not detected' or keeps the median, and differential testing pushes the package toward that opinion. (2) The factor of a gene with two curve points: the natural fix of 3.1 deletes the cap everywhere, and a solver who notices 2.5's three-point bound tends to fall back to 2.0. Keeping either value requires adding a branch that reproduces today's step. A solver that audits every defined figure for inputs outside its rule and asks what today's code does there gets both.
